headline: Secure Mandatory Rogers Pass Permits and Park Entry
reservation: Visitors require a valid Parks Canada Discovery Pass or daily entry fee to access the park. Specific winter and spring access to many slopes is strictly regulated under the Winter Permitting System to manage avalanche risks; summer hiking access may vary based on trail maintenance and grizzly activity. Always verify current trail closures and localized permitting requirements via the Parks Canada website before arrival.

days.title: Ancient Cedars and Selkirk History

stops.name: Hemlock Grove Boardwalk
stops.detail: Walk through an accessible tract of old-growth inland temperate rainforest featuring ancient western hemlocks.

stops.name: Rogers Pass Discovery Centre
stops.detail: Explore the history of the Canadian Pacific Railway and the engineering feats required to navigate this steep mountain corridor.

days.driving: Allow 1 to 2 hours for mountain transit; conditions vary
days.note: Expect steep gradients and heavy transport traffic along the Trans-Canada Highway.

days.title: Glacial Vistas and Alpine Trails

stops.name: Great Glacier Trail
stops.detail: Ascend toward the Illecillewaet Glacier’s edge to see the remnants of the ice that spurred early mountain tourism.

stops.name: Meeting of the Waters
stops.detail: View the convergence of Asulkan Brook and the Illecillewaet River near the historic ruins of Glacier House.

days.driving: Minimal road travel between local trailheads; allow for parking transitions
days.note: Trail availability depends heavily on the seasonal snowmelt, typically clear by mid-July.

days.title: Mountain Summits and Pass Views

stops.name: Asulkan Valley
stops.detail: Hike through u-shaped glacial valleys toward high-altitude waterfalls and moraines.

stops.name: Loop Brook Trail
stops.detail: Examine the massive stone pillars that once supported railway trestles over the rugged terrain.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local transfers and return toward Golden; conditions vary
days.note: The weather at Rogers Pass can change rapidly; maintain a flexible pace.

intel.title: Illecillewaet Trailhead Hub
intel.text: Parking at the Illecillewaet area serves multiple major trails and tends to reach capacity during summer weekends. Secondary lots at Loop Brook provide alternative access for shorter historical walks.

intel.title: Connectivity Gaps
intel.text: Cellular reception is largely unavailable throughout the mountain interior and trail systems. The Discovery Centre at Rogers Pass offers the most reliable point for emergency communications.

intel.title: Gateway Provisions
intel.text: There are no refueling stations within the park boundaries. Travelers should top up tanks in Revelstoke or Golden before entering the Rogers Pass corridor.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Maintenance
intel.text: Construction delays on the Trans-Canada Highway are common during the short summer maintenance window. Check DriveBC for real-time updates on bridge work or lane closures.

intel.title: Winter Permitting Areas
intel.text: From late autumn through spring, vast areas of the park are restricted to facilitate avalanche control. Public entry into these zones requires a specific daily permit and safety briefing.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Kelowna (YLW) and stop in Revelstoke for mountain-grade groceries and fuel before the climb to the pass.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for the highway, but high-clearance cars are recommended for those sensitive to steep mountain grades and heavy rain.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset from the Rogers Pass Monument offers dramatic shadows across the Hermit Range, though timing fluctuates significantly by month.
